This suit of the plaintiff is for permanent injunction restraining the defendants No.1 to 6 from interfering/disturbing with his peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property bearing school premises No.230, 3rd Stage, 3rd Division, 6th Main Road, situated inside the compound of the Government High School, Saneguruvanahalli, Basaweshwaranagara, Bengaluru,
measuring East to West 10 feet and North to South 15 feet, consisting of one hall, kitchen, bath room built with bricks and cement, A.C. sheet roofing, door and windows of iron.

The plaintiff's case in brief are as follows :
2(a).
The plaintiff has filed this suit for permanent injunction.
The father of plaintiff late Sri.Muniyappa rendered the service in Saneguruvanahalli Government High School as a Watchmen on honorary basis.
His father was died on 23/12/2009.

Thereafter, the plaintiff continued the service of his father as Watchman and taking care and safety of the school and also doing the work instructed by the school staffs,
educational officers, teachers etc.,. 2(b).
From the period of his father, the school authorities and educational department have provided an accommodation to his father in a portion of school premise i.e., suit schedule shed.
Subsequently, the plaintiff and his family members continued, the school authorities as well as educational officers recognized his continuation in the schedule premise.
The wife of the plaintiff OS.No. 2431/2024 Smt.Jayalakshmamma is working as Aaya in the High School and she had obtained Gas connection and Bank account in respect of schedule premises.
2(c). The defendant No.1 and 2 by influence and pressure from the politically motivated persons attempted to disturb and interfere with the plaintiff's possession over the schedule premises.

The 1 st defendant in the month of December 2023, along with defendant No.2 created nuisance and threatened the plaintiff and his family members to dispossess them from the schedule premises and other defendants have not solved their problems.
If the plaintiff and his family members are thrown out from the schedule premises, they will be on the street without food and shelter.

2(d). The defendants have issued notice to the plaintiff and made an attempt to disturb the physical possession and tried to remove the shed stayed in the OS.No.
2431/2024 schedule property.
The complaint was lodged to jurisdictional police, but they refused to receive the same.
Hence, filed this suit.
3. The defendants have filed written statement by contending that the plaintiff's suit is not maintainable.
The plaintiff's wife Smt.Jayalakshmamma has been appointed as Aaya on temporary/contract basis on 17/08/1995 as Group-D employee at Government Model Primary School, Saneguruvanahalli.
The plaintiff is presently residing in the school premises unauthorized manner causing trouble to academic activities of the school.
The plaintiff and his wife claiming that they own the above said room of the school premises.
The plaintiff has not been appointed as Watchman either from the School or Educational Department.

Apart from Smt.Jayalakshmamma,

The plaintiff has not approached the Court with clean hands.
The Government Mode Primary School and Government High School of Saneguruvanahalli for the benefit of children and school got sanctioned 8 rooms under 'Viveka Shala Yojane'.
The defendant school has issued notice to the plaintiff to vacate the shed and he requested 3 months time to vacate the same.
The process of construction of the building has started and at that time, the present suit is filed and children academic progress is damaging.
The children have no place to sit or for class process.
In the SDMC and parents meeting dated 18/12/2023, decided to serve the notice to the plaintiff to vacate the shed.
The plaintiff has no right, title and interest over the schedule premises.
The defendant No.1 and 2 have no personal interest and no enmity against the plaintiff, they have been made parties in their individual capacity and prayed for dismissal of the suit.

On the basis of the above said pleadings, this Court has framed 5 issues are as follows :
ISSUES 1) Whether the Plaintiff proves that, he has been in lawful possession and enjoyment over the suit schedule premises ?
2) Whether the plaintiff proves that the defendants are interfering with his peaceful possession and enjoyment over the suit schedule premises?

3) Whether the plaintiff proves that the School and Educational Department have given accommodation in the schedule premises to his father for rendering services as watchman and he continued rendering service as watchman and staying in the schedule premises?
4) Whether the plaintiff is entitled for relief of permanent injunction?
5) What order or decree?
5. The plaintiff examined himself as PW.1.
Exs.P-1 to P-10 documents are marked.
On behalf of the defendants, defendant No.2 examined as PW.1.
Exs.D-1 to D-27 documents are marked.

8(a).
The plaintiff in his oral evidence deposed as per the plaint averments that he is residing in the suit schedule premises with his wife.
His father Muniyappa was rendering service of Watchman of the school premises.
After death of his father, he OS.No. 2431/2024 continued as Watchman on honorary basis without any salary.
From 1983 father of plaintiff was rendering service.
The defendants all of a sudden issued a notice for vacating the premises and interfering with his peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property, has has no accommodation to reside.
As such, he filed a suit for permanent injunction against the defendants.

9. The DW.1 - 2nd defendant Head Master of Government High School, Saneguruvanahalli,
Basaveshwaranagar, Bangalore, deposed the evidence as per the written statement contention that the plaintiff's wife was appointed as temporary/contract basis as Aya on 01-06-1995 and working as 'D' Group employee at Government Model Primary school, Saneguruvanahalli, receiving salary from Education department.

The defendants or the Education department at no point of time appointed the plaintiff or his father for rendering service in the school.
9(a). The plaintiff who was running petty shop in the school premises in unauthorized manner.
After noticing the same by the higher authorities, petty shop was closed as it was affecting the health and academic activities of the children.
The premises in which the plaintiff and his wife have unauthorizedly occupied do not have separate way to ingress and egress from the shed, which is official school gate for children convenience.

Under "Viveka Shala Yojane"
eight rooms were sanctioned.

As per the sanction of eight rooms for the purpose of construction, the premises in which the plaintiff and his wife is in OS.No. 2431/2024 occupation is required to be vacated and issued notice to the plaintiff's wife to vacate the shed, the plaintiff has sought 3 months time to vacate the premises.
The meeting of SDMC and parent association was also convened, in which the plaintiff, his wife and son were also participated and did not vacate the premises.
For construction of new 8 rooms, three old dilapidated rooms have been demolished.
The school has no place for children to sit after class room closes.

10. The counsel for the plaintiff in support of his submissions argued that the plaintiff and his wife are in occupation of suit schedule property.
The plaintiff's father since from 1983 was running service OS.No. 2431/2024 in the school as per the advise of the Villagers, as there was illegal activities were going on in the school premises.
The plaintiff's father was asked to look after the school premises.
Since then the father of plaintiff was stayed in the suit schedule premises and rendering service to the school as honorary as Watchman.

The counsel further submits that after the death of father of plaintiff, the plaintiff continued to stay in the suit schedule premises with his wife,
who is also working as Aya in the very same school appointed by the Education department. 10(a).
The counsel submits that the defendants all of a sudden issued notice demanding the plaintiff to vacate the suit schedule premises and making illegal demand.
The plaintiff has no other accommodation to stay.
The suit schedule premises/shed has separate ingress and egress.
The demolition of shed is not required for construction of 8 new class rooms to the children.
The photographs are created by the OS.No. 2431/2024 defendants for the purpose of the case to show that the school has no class rooms and children are sitting outside the school.

The counsel further submitted that the plaintiff in order to show the possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property since long time, the bank pass book, gas bill address are shown as a suit schedule property.

The photograph of Exs.P-8 and P-9 series would show the plaintiff and his wife are staying in the suit schedule premises without any hindrance and they have right to continue in the suit schedule premises.
The defendants unnecessarily interfering and prayed to decree the suit.
11. The learned D.G.P. on behalf of the defendants submitted that the plaintiff is not at all connected to defendant school.
His wife is working in the school appointed by the Education department as Aya.
There is no post called Watchman in the school.
The School or Education department have not appointed either father of the plaintiff or plaintiff as a Watchman to render service in the school.
It is further submitted that the plaintiff has not placed any material to show that his father was rendering service in the school as Watchman and thereafter plaintiff.
The wife of plaintiff was appointed as Aya in the year 1995 and she was transferred to this school subsequently.

It is further submitted that the Government had sanctioned 8 rooms under "Viveka Shala Yojane"
an amount of Rs.1 crore was sanctioned.
The dilapidated 3 class rooms have been demolished for the purpose of construction of 8 rooms.

The children presently have no class rooms and they are sitting outside the class rooms in the school premises,
affecting their educational activities.

The counsel submits that thought plaintiff and his wife are OS.No. 2431/2024 staying in the suit schedule premises, their occupation Muniraju M vs Reeni on 4 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40571489/
6 is unauthorized without any authority either by the School or department. 11(b).

The counsel further submits that utmost the plaintiff and his wife staying in the school premises as a licencee on permission, once license or permission are revoked, they have no right or authority to continue.
The plaintiff's wife is not party to the suit.
She has not filed any suit.
The plaintiff is not connected with the suit.

The plaintiff has not approached the Court with clean hands and he is not entitled for discretionary relief of permanent injunction and prayed for dismissal of suit.
12.

After considering the submissions, it is necessary to appreciate the oral and documentary evidence on record to find out whether the plaintiff is in lawful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property, whether the defendants are OS.No. 2431/2024 interfering with his lawful possession and enjoyment and entitle for injunction.

The plaintiff in support of his oral evidence, he relied upon Exs.P-1 to P-4 are the copies of complaint addressed to Block Educational Officer,
Commissioner of Education department, Principal Secretary of Education department and Director of Education department, which were addressed just prior to filing of the suit making allegation against defendant No.2 and other defendants regarding interfering and insisting him to vacate the suit schedule premises and he also stated that his father was rendering service as Watchman in the school from 1981-82 and thereafter, he is continuing in the suit schedule premises and rendering service to the school as Watchman on honorary basis without salary.
13. The plaintiff produced Exs.P-5 and P-6 Gas bills for the month of January and April 2024 standing in the name of Jayalakshmamma - wife of plaintiff.
OS.No. 2431/2024 Ex.P-7 is the Bank pass book in respect of suit schedule property standing in the name of Jayalakshmamma.
Ex.P-8 series photographs and Ex.P-9 photographs.

However, the plaintiff has not produced 65-B certificate in respect of Ex.P-9 series photographs and Ex.P-8 photographs negatives are not produced, which were marked with objections of defendants subject to 65-B certificate and negatives.
So far as the plaintiff has not produced negatives of Ex.P-8 series photos and certificate under Sec.65-B in respect of Ex.P-9 series photographs
. In the absence of those material negatives and certificates, Exs.P-8 and P-9 photos cannot be admitted in evidence.
Therefore, which are excluded from relying upon by the plaintiff.
14. The defendants in respect of their contentions relied upon Ex.D-1 - Reply given by the plaintiff on 04-04-2024 requesting 3 months time to vacate the premises.
Ex.D-2 is student strength in Government OS.No. 2431/2024 Model Primary School, Saneguruvanahalli, for the year 2024-25.
It would disclose that from 1 st to 7th standard, in all 304 students are studying in the said school, out of which 139 are girl student and 165 are boy students.

In para 13 PW.1 deposed that there is no Government Circular having appointed him in Saneguruvanahalli Government School and no documents are produced by him to show that he is working in said school.
He admits that there is no provision for the school for appointment of Watchman.
According to him elders of the Villagers asked him to maintain school to prevent illegal activities, which were going on the school premises.
He admits the Villagers or School authorities have not filed any complaint in respect of illegal activities in the school premises.
He admits, the Government OS.No. 2431/2024 or School authorities have not given any order in writing authorizing him to stay in the school premises.
He also admits he has not produced any authorization given by the Villagers to stay in the school premises.

That as on the date of joining school by her she came to know that plaintiff and his wife occupied one of the school premises room.

sentences.text: After appreciating the evidence on record, it is not in dispute the plaintiff and his wife Jayalakshmamma are staying in the suit schedule premises.

However, there is no document to substantiate the contention of the plaintiff that during 1981-82 on wards his father Muniyappa was rendering service as Watchman and after his death the plaintiff has continued to render service in the school on honorary basis without salary.
PW.1 explicitly admitted there are no documents to show that he and his father was appointed by the Government or School authorities to render service as Watchman in the School.
PW.1 contention that the Villagers have asked his father and him to render service in the School to prevent illegal activities in the school premises.
However, to show that there were illegal activities were going on in the school premises, there is no piece of paper.

Secondly, there is no material that the Villagers have asked either the plaintiff or his father to look after the school premises OS.No. 2431/2024 to prevent illegal activities in the school premises.
The Villagers have no right or authority either orally or writing to authorize the plaintiff and his father to render service in the school.
First of all there is no material that the Villagers have authorized the plaintiff to render service.
The SDMC School development management works were established in the year 2001.
Earlier to that Villagers have no voice in respect of school premises.
The plaintiff has not produced any document to show that from 1981-82 on wards his father was rendering service in the school and stayed in the suit schedule premises.
There is no material on record that the plaintiff and his wife are staying in the suit schedule premises from 1983 on wards.
Admittedly, the plaintiff's wife Jayalakshmamma is working as Aya in the Government Primary School, Saneguruvanahalli.
PW.1 deposed that his wife has transferred to said school and working from 18-12-2003.
The plaintiff has not placed any material that he is staying in the suit schedule premises from 1982-83.
The gas bills and bank pass book are recent documents.

Therefore, the plaintiff and his wife are not staying in the suit schedule premises for long time, on the other hand,
in all probabilities after plaintiff's wife transferred to defendant school appeared to have staying in the suit schedule premises without any authority or permission from the school or Government Education department.
Therefore, the possession of plaintiff and his wife in the suit schedule premises is not lawful and it is unauthorize and illegal.
18. The counsel for the plaintiff in the cross- examination of DW.1 has suggested that the plaintiff and his wife are staying in the suit schedule premises from 1996 on permissive possession.

If said OS.No. 2431/2024 suggestion is taken into consideration, assuming that the School or Education department has permitted the plaintiff and his wife to stay in the suit schedule premises, it is only on permission as that of a licensee.
Once permission is revoked by issuing notice, the plaintiff and his wife have no business to stay in the suit schedule premises.
19. PW.1 admitted there are 600 children are studying in the school.
Due to shortage of school rooms under "Viveka Shala Yojane" 8 rooms are sanctioned for construction.

The work order and Muniraju M vs Reeni on 4 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40571489/
9 estimation order are also placed before the Court, which would show Rs.83.40 lakhs was sanctioned for construction of 8 rooms.
The existing 3 dilapidated rooms are demolished for the purpose of construction of 8 rooms.
The photographs would depicts presently the children are sitting outside the school building and classes are being conducted due to shortage of school rooms.
The suit schedule premises is situated in the place where the proposed 8 class rooms are to be constructed.
Therefore, the existence of shed for the purpose of construction of 8 rooms is an obstruction.
As per the work order the construction of rooms have to be completed before 28-08-2024.
But, it has not been carried out due to obstruction by the plaintiff and his wife by not vacating the premises.

Therefore, if the construction is not completed within the financial year, there is every chance of lapse of the amount which was granted for construction of class rooms for welfare of the children in the interest of their academic activities.
The issuance of notice by the defendants to the plaintiff's wife to vacate the shed in the school premises cannot be termed as interference.
The plaintiff himself is not in lawful possession of suit schedule premises.

The wife of plaintiff being employee of 'D' group working in the same school, not vacating the premises so as to OS.No. 2431/2024 accommodate construction of 8 rooms for academic activities of the children amounts to misconduct.
20. The plaintiff has not placed any material to hold that he is in lawful possession of suit schedule property.
There is no material since from the time of his father he has been in occupation of suit schedule premises.
The plaintiff has suppressed the material facts.
The suit for permanent injunction, it is a discretionary relief.
The person who approaches the Court must come with clean hands without any suppression.
The plaintiff has not able to establish that he is in lawful possession of suit schedule premises.
His possession is unlawful and unauthorized.
The defendant school has issued notice to vacate the premises.
If the suit is not decreed, the defendants would be put to irreparable loss and injury, there is every chance of lapse of huge amount sanctioned for construction of 8 class rooms.

Therefore, by considering the interest of children OS.No. 2431/2024 studying around 600 students, if the injunction is granted to protect the plaintiff to stay in the schedule premises would affect the educational activities of the children.
Permanent injunction cannot be granted against the true owner.
Therefore, the plaintiff is not entitled for injunction.
Accordingly, answered issues No.1 to 4 in the Negative.
21. ISSUE NO.5:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 to 4, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The suit of the plaintiff is dismissed with costs.
Draw decree accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
2(d). The defendants have issued notice to the plaintiff and made an attempt to disturb the physical possession and tried to remove the shed stayed in the OS.No.
2431/2024 schedule property.
The complaint was lodged to jurisdictional police, but they refused to receive the same.
Hence, filed this suit.
The defendant school has issued notice to the plaintiff to vacate the shed and he requested 3 months time to vacate the same.
The children have no place to sit or for class process.
In the SDMC and parents meeting dated 18/12/2023, decided to serve the notice to the plaintiff to vacate the shed.
The plaintiff has no right, title and interest over the schedule premises.
The defendant No.1 and 2 have no personal interest and no enmity against the plaintiff, they have been made parties in their individual capacity and prayed for dismissal of the suit.
After death of his father, he OS.No. 2431/2024 continued as Watchman on honorary basis without any salary.
As such, he filed a suit for permanent injunction against the defendants.
opennyai_summary.issue:
On the basis of the above said pleadings, this Court has framed 5 issues are as follows :
ISSUES 1) Whether the Plaintiff proves that, he has been in lawful possession and enjoyment over the suit schedule premises ?
2) Whether the plaintiff proves that the defendants are interfering with his peaceful possession and enjoyment over the suit schedule premises?
3) Whether the plaintiff proves that the School and Educational Department have given accommodation in the schedule premises to his father for rendering services as watchman and he continued rendering service as watchman and staying in the schedule premises?
4) Whether the plaintiff is entitled for relief of permanent injunction?
5) What order or decree?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
However, there is no document to substantiate the contention of the plaintiff that during 1981-82 on wards his father Muniyappa was rendering service as Watchman and after his death the plaintiff has continued to render service in the school on honorary basis without salary.
However, to show that there were illegal activities were going on in the school premises, there is no piece of paper.
Secondly, there is no material that the Villagers have asked either the plaintiff or his father to look after the school premises OS.No. 2431/2024 to prevent illegal activities in the school premises.
The Villagers have no right or authority either orally or writing to authorize the plaintiff and his father to render service in the school.
First of all there is no material that the Villagers have authorized the plaintiff to render service.
Therefore, the possession of plaintiff and his wife in the suit schedule premises is not lawful and it is unauthorize and illegal.
Therefore, the existence of shed for the purpose of construction of 8 rooms is an obstruction.
As per the work order the construction of rooms have to be completed before 28-08-2024.
But, it has not been carried out due to obstruction by the plaintiff and his wife by not vacating the premises.
Therefore, if the construction is not completed within the financial year, there is every chance of lapse of the amount which was granted for construction of class rooms for welfare of the children in the interest of their academic activities.
The issuance of notice by the defendants to the plaintiff's wife to vacate the shed in the school premises cannot be termed as interference.
The wife of plaintiff being employee of 'D' group working in the same school, not vacating the premises so as to OS.No. 2431/2024 accommodate construction of 8 rooms for academic activities of the children amounts to misconduct.
20. The plaintiff has not placed any material to hold that he is in lawful possession of suit schedule property.
There is no material since from the time of his father he has been in occupation of suit schedule premises.
The plaintiff has suppressed the material facts.
The suit for permanent injunction, it is a discretionary relief.
The person who approaches the Court must come with clean hands without any suppression.
The plaintiff has not able to establish that he is in lawful possession of suit schedule premises.
His possession is unlawful and unauthorized.
If the suit is not decreed, the defendants would be put to irreparable loss and injury, there is every chance of lapse of huge amount sanctioned for construction of 8 class rooms.
Therefore, by considering the interest of children OS.No. 2431/2024 studying around 600 students, if the injunction is granted to protect the plaintiff to stay in the schedule premises would affect the educational activities of the children.
opennyai_summary.decision:
The defendant school has issued notice to vacate the premises.
Permanent injunction cannot be granted against the true owner.
Therefore, the plaintiff is not entitled for injunction.
Accordingly, answered issues No.1 to 4 in the Negative.
In view of my findings on issues No.1 to 4, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The suit of the plaintiff is dismissed with costs.
Draw decree accordingly.
